quote: Example 1. Let F be some DFR distribution. As the DFR class is included in the DFRA class, we may apply Corollaries 7 and 8 to obtain ordering relations between different record values. ... Take (n, k) = (10, 5). Applying Corollary 7(i), one gets R10^{(5)} ⪯icx Rm^{(j)} whenever m > 10, j > 5 and m > 2j. This identifies the shaded area in Figure 1. To this region we may add the points that verify condition (i) in Corollary 8, represented by the points above the line j = m/2 , where R10^{(5)} ⪯ss Rm^{(j)} will hold.
compared: numeric parameter region for icx/ss ordering of R10^(5) vs Rm^(j)

hypotheses.text: F DFR; (n,k) = (10,5); m > 10, j > 5, m > 2j for icx; Cor 8(i) points for ss

conclusion.direction: R_{10}^{(5)} ⪯icx R_m^{(j)} on region m > 2j; ⪯ss on additional points above j = m/2
